original_question: Can semi-analytic models with radio-mode AGN feedback achieve quantitative agreement with the observed star-formation histories of massive elliptical galaxies, rather than only reproducing the qualitative trend that more massive ellipticals have shorter star-formation time-scales?
target_in_paper: A good quantitative agreement has not been shown yet and is complicated by large uncertainties associated to star formation histories extracted from observed galaxy spectra.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies that semi-analytic galaxy formation models incorporating radio-mode AGN feedback qualitatively reproduce the observed trend that more massive elliptical galaxies have shorter star-formation time-scales but have not demonstrated quantitative agreement with the star-formation histories inferred from observations.
missing_details: Specify the metric for 'quantitative agreement', such as mass-weighted stellar ages or star-formation time-scales derived from model versus observed spectra
Define 'massive elliptical galaxies' in terms of stellar mass or halo mass ranges considered
Identify the observational data set and spectral fitting method used to derive star-formation histories, including associated uncertainties
Clarify which specific semi-analytic model implementations are under consideration (e.g. Croton et al. 2006 or Bower et al. 2006 radio-mode feedback recipes)
Specify the redshift or epoch at which the model–observation comparison is performed (e.g. z≈0)
refined_question: To what quantitative extent do semi-analytic ΛCDM galaxy formation models that implement a radio-mode AGN feedback prescription (e.g. as in Croton et al. 2006 or Bower et al. 2006) reproduce the observed star-formation histories of local (z≈0) massive elliptical galaxies (defined as those with stellar mass M_*≳10^11 M_⊙), when model-predicted mass-weighted ages and star-formation time-scales are directly compared to those derived from spectral fitting analyses of observed galaxy spectra?
justification: This refined question directly targets the open problem stated in the 'RECENT SUCCESSES AND OPEN PROBLEMS' section of the paper (page 3), where De Lucia et al. note the lack of demonstrated quantitative agreement between models with radio-mode AGN feedback and observed star-formation histories in massive ellipticals. It adds necessary definitions and scope restrictions—such as the mass range, model implementations, observational methods, and redshift—to make the question fully self-contained and faithful to the paper’s intent.
